summary: 《金银岛》作者史蒂文森虽广为人知，文学地位却曾下滑。文章追问冒险小说为何难获严肃评价，并从创作和对后世作家的影响重新衡量他的成就。
logic: 批评界对冒险小说的偏见
追踪对其他作家的影响

paragraphs.brief: 苏格兰作家罗伯特·路易斯·史蒂文森在南太平洋萨摩亚岛上去世已经100多年了，看来时间对史蒂文森的记忆并不好。
sentences: It is more than 100 years since the death of the Scottish writer Robert Louis Stevenson on the South Pacific island of Samoa, and it seems that time has not been kind to Stevenson’s memory.
苏格兰作家罗伯特·路易斯·史蒂文森在南太平洋萨摩亚岛上去世已经100多年了，看来时间对史蒂文森的记忆并不好。
Immediately after his death, his family and friends set to work to fashion the legend of Robert Louis Stevenson, or R.
他死后，家人和朋友立刻开始制作罗伯特·路易斯·史蒂文森的传奇
L.
S., as he became known, one of the few writers familiar from his initials alone.
S，正如他所知道的，少数几个作者之一熟悉从他的首字母。
Subsequent works of biography then turned him into a writer of almost religious importance.
随后的传记作品使他成为一位几乎具有宗教重要性的作家。
One example was literary critic Balfour, who in 1901 portrayed Stevenson’s family as ministering angels to the dying genius during his final illness.
文学评论家Balfour就是一个例子，他在1901年把Stevenson的家人描绘成在最后的疾病中为垂死天才服务的天使。
Similarly, the biographer Crouch absurdly overstated Stevenson’s significance by placing him in the same company as those most revered names in English literature: Shakespeare and Keats.
同样地，传记家Crauch 荒谬地夸大了史蒂文森的重要性，将他与英国文学中最受敬重的名字：莎士比亚和济慈放在同一家公司。
The reaction to this nonsense was a number of highly critical assessments of Stevenson’s legacy in the 1920s.
对这一无稽之谈的反应是对史蒂文森在1920年代遗留下来的诸多批评性评估。

paragraphs.brief: 但史蒂文森工作的一些方面，直到最近，都与更平衡的评估背道而驰。
sentences: Normally, the critical pendulum can be relied on to swing back again, but there are several aspects of Stevenson’s work that have, until recently, acted against a more balanced appraisal.
但史蒂文森工作的一些方面，直到最近，都与更平衡的评估背道而驰。
First is the allegation that Stevenson was a mere master of linguistic fireworks, who lacked moral depth.
首先，有人指控史蒂文森只是语言烟火大师，缺乏道德深度。
Some critics accused him of being a literary charlatan, of juggling words very prettily to strike effects which overawed an ignorant public, and served to distract from the inadequacy of his ideas.
一些批评者指责他是一个文学的骗子，用极巧妙的言辞来打击那些推翻无知公众的影响，并分散了他的思想的不适当性。

paragraphs.brief: 长期以来，人们一直对冒险故事抱有偏见，认为它是道德严肃性的适当媒介，这种偏见今天仍然具有极大的影响力。
sentences: Then there has long been a prejudice against the adventure story as the proper medium for deep moral seriousness, a prejudice which is still extremely influential today.
长期以来，人们一直对冒险故事抱有偏见，认为它是道德严肃性的适当媒介，这种偏见今天仍然具有极大的影响力。
It seems that we can accept that an adventure film can successfully express profound moral truths, but we reject the same idea for a book.
似乎我们可以接受冒险电影能够成功地表达深刻的道德真理，但我们拒绝对一本书的同样想法。

The absurdity of this becomes apparent when we think of writers like Joseph Conrad and Graham Greene, but it is no use pretending that this bias against adventure stories is not part of our high culture.
我们想到约瑟夫·康拉德和格雷厄姆·格林这样的作家时，这件事的荒谬性变得很明显，但假装这种对冒险故事的偏见并不是我们高尚文化的一部分是没有用的。
A further problem is that Stevenson has often not found favour in the land of his birth because his conservatism so often collides with the strong radical tradition in Scotland.
另一个问题是，史蒂文森在出生地往往得不到青睐，因为他的保守主义常常与苏格兰的强大激进传统相冲突。
His many escapist stories and preference for living abroad have led to accusations that he camouflaged Scotland’s problems.
他有许多逃避国外生活的故事和偏好，导致有人指控他掩盖苏格兰的问题。
Lastly, the high adventure of Stevenson’s own lifestyle has sometimes obscured his output, his life a greater story than any he could devise.
最后，史蒂文森自身生活方式的高度冒险有时掩盖了他的产出，他的生活比他所能设计的任何故事都更加美好。
This was precisely what his friends feared would happen towards the end of his short life: his art might be overwhelmed by the drama of life in Samoa.
这正是他的朋友担心在短命即将结束的时候会发生的事情：他的艺术可能会被萨摩亚的生活戏剧所淹没。

paragraphs.brief: 其后果之一是史蒂文森对其他作家的影响常常被忽视。
sentences: One consequence of this has been that Stevenson’s influence on other writers has too often been neglected.
其后果之一是史蒂文森对其他作家的影响常常被忽视。
The writer and poet Oscar Wilde was deeply influenced by Stevenson, even though he declared that Stevenson would have produced better work if he had lived in London rather than Samoa.
作家兼诗人奥斯卡·王尔德深受史蒂文森的影响，尽管他宣称，史蒂文生如果在伦敦而不是萨摩亚居住，他本可以做得更好。
Stevenson tends to stick in the throat even of those writers who would like to spit him out, such as Shaw, who claimed to have learned from him that the romantic hero is always mocked by reality.
史蒂文森倾向于坚持在喉咙即使那些作家谁想吐他出来，例如肖，谁声称已经从他学到浪漫英雄总是被现实嘲笑。

Likewise, the writer Galsworthy, who began as a determined critic, later changed his mind and said that the superiority of Stevenson over the novelist Hardy was that Stevenson was all life and Hardy all death.
同样，作家加尔斯沃西(Galsworthy)一开始是一位坚定的批评家，后来他改变了主意，他说史蒂文森比小说家哈迪优越的是史蒂文生生，哈代死。

The influence on the novelist Chesterton would also repay detailed study, for it was through him that Stevenson has managed to cross the ages, emerging as an influence on the modernist movement and our own contemporary Latin American school of “magical realism”.
对小说家切斯特顿的影响也将回报他的详细研究，因为史蒂文森通过他成功地跨越了时代，成为了对现代主义运动和我们当代拉丁美洲“磁现实主义”学校的影响。

paragraphs.brief: 即使我们没有看到这位伟大的苏格兰作家的极大兴趣重新出现，但人们希望读者们回到罗伯特·路易·史蒂文森的伟大故事中，重新评估这个被忽视的天才。
sentences: When making an assessment of his life and work one question must inevitably be asked: was Robert Louis Stevenson Scotland’s greatest writer of English prose?
在评估他的生活和工作时，必然要问一个问题：罗伯特·路易斯·史蒂文森是苏格兰最伟大的英文诗篇作家吗？

For most commentators this honour falls to Sir Walter Scott, author of Ivanhoe among many other classic novels, and it is true that in terms of craftsmanship, precision and the ability to minutely regulate language to create the desired effect, Scott takes the prize.
对于大多数评论者来说，这一荣誉落在了Walter Scott爵士身上，他是伊万霍的作者，他是许多其他经典小说的作者。确实，在手工艺、精准和对语言进行微调以创造理想效果的能力方面，Scott获得了奖赏。

However, this is not the same thing at all as inherent talent; by way of comparison one may take the example of the two great Russian composers Shostakovich and Prokofiev, of whom the former had learned more precise skills of execution but the latter’s intrinsic genius was greater, and so it seems to be with Scott and Stevenson.
然而，这与天生的才华完全不同；相比之下，可以举两位伟大的俄罗斯作曲家Shostakovich和Prokofiev为例，前者学到了更精确的处决技能，但后者的内在才华则更大，因此，史考特和史蒂文森似乎也具有这种天赋。

Admittedly, Scott’s detailed style does permit his stories to explore levels of tragedy that are beyond Stevenson’s reach, but in this regard they have the musty smell of the museum, somehow artificial and removed from modern day reality.
诚然，斯科特的精细风格确实使他的故事能够探索史蒂文森所无法触及的悲剧程度，但在这方面，他们有着博物馆的杂音，不知何故是人为的，并脱离了现代现实。

On the other hand, Stevenson’s skill with plotting and narrative gives his books a timeless quality, so that they still live today, and Stevenson was also the shrewder judge of behaviour and psychology.
但史蒂文森的阴谋和叙事技巧给了他的书一个永恒的品质，这样他们仍然活在今天，史蒂文森也是行为和心理学的精明判断者。

For example, his compelling descriptions of a man with a split personality in The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde have proved so accessible and accurate that the expression “Jekyll and Hyde” has entered common English usage.
例如，他在Jekyll博士和Hyde先生的《奇特案例》中对一个人格分裂的人所作的令人信服的描述证明，“Jekyell和Hyde”的表达方式非常容易理解和准确，已进入了英国的通用用语。

Even if we do not see a revival of critical interest in this great Scottish writer, it is to be hoped that readers go back to Robert Louis Stevenson’s magnificent stories and reassess this neglected genius.
即使我们没有看到这位伟大的苏格兰作家的极大兴趣重新出现，但人们希望读者们回到罗伯特·路易·史蒂文森的伟大故事中，重新评估这个被忽视的天才。

items.en: In the opinion of the writer, the biographers Balfour and Crouch
items.zh: 作者如何看待传记作家鲍尔弗和克劳奇对史蒂文森的评价？
correct: elevated Stevenson above his true status as a writer.
他们高估了史蒂文森作为作家的地位。

items.en: What is the writer’s main point about Stevenson in the second paragraph?
items.zh: 第二段中，作者要说明关于史蒂文森的哪一点？
correct: Critics argued that his style covered up his faults.
批评家认为，他的文风掩盖了他的不足。

items.en: According to the writer, the adventure story
items.zh: 在作者看来，冒险故事这种体裁有何用途？
correct: can be used by writers to tell moral stories.
作家可以借它讲述带有道德寓意的故事。

items.en: What point does the writer make about Stevenson and Scotland?
items.zh: 作者如何描述史蒂文森与苏格兰的关系？
correct: His ideas contrasted with those of many Scots.
他的观念与许多苏格兰人的观念不同。

items.en: According to the writer, Stevenson’s own lifestyle
items.zh: 作者如何评价史蒂文森本人的生活方式？
correct: attracted more attention than his books.
它比他的著作吸引了更多关注。

items.en: Although Oscar Wilde admired Stevenson’s work, he believed Stevenson could have written something better.
items.zh: 奥斯卡·王尔德虽然欣赏史蒂文森的作品，但认为他本可以写出更好的作品。
items.why: 原文说王尔德深受史蒂文森影响，同时认为史蒂文森若住在伦敦，作品会更好。欣赏与认为作品仍有提升空间可以同时成立。

items.en: Stevenson encouraged Oscar Wilde to start writing.
items.zh: 史蒂文森鼓励过奥斯卡·王尔德开始写作。
items.why: 王尔德受到史蒂文森作品的影响，与史蒂文森亲自鼓励他开始写作是两件事。作者只陈述了前者。

items.en: Galsworthy had greater respect for Hardy than Stevenson.
items.zh: 与史蒂文森相比，高尔斯华绥更敬重哈代。
items.why: 高尔斯华绥后来明确肯定史蒂文森胜过哈代。题干将他最终更推崇的作家说反了。

items.en: More research is needed regarding Stevenson’s influence on Chesterton.
items.zh: 史蒂文森对切斯特顿的影响还有待进一步研究。
items.why: 作者说史蒂文森对切斯特顿的影响“值得详细研究”，正对应题干所说还需要进一步研究。

clauses: It is more than 100 years since the death of the Scottish writer Robert Louis Stevenson on the South Pacific island of Samoa, and it seems ….
“that time has not been kind to Stevenson’s memory”补足 seems 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 seems 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
One example was literary critic Balfour, ….
“who in 1901 portrayed Stevenson’s family as ministering angels to the dying genius during his final illness”修饰前面的 Balfour。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 Balfour，再把修饰信息接回主句。
